title: Sentinel Protocol Defensive Operations: Incident Response with AWS CloudWatch Logs
objectives: Understand the Sentinel Protocol and its role in defensive operations
Configure AWS CloudWatch Logs to detect security events
Create an incident response plan using AWS CloudWatch Events

mission_brief.briefing: Your security team has been tasked with implementing the Sentinel Protocol to enhance defensive operations. You will work closely with AWS to configure CloudWatch Logs and create an incident response plan.
rules_of_engagement: Do not proceed without completing all setup and configuration steps
Use only official AWS documentation for solution guidance
Test your configuration thoroughly before declaring success

content.concept: The Sentinel Protocol is a proactive approach to defensive operations that emphasizes incident detection, response, and recovery using cloud-based services. In this lesson, we focus on using AWS CloudWatch Logs to detect security events and creating an incident response plan with AWS CloudWatch Events.
content.walkthrough:
Configure AWS CloudFormation to create a new stack for Sentinel Protocol implementation. Then, use the AWS CLI to configure CloudWatch Logs and set up a simple event pattern in CloudWatch Events.

Expansion: Walk through expected command outputs, common failure modes, and a verification loop (change → verify → record).
checkpoints: Verify that your CloudWatch Log group is created correctly
Ensure that your incident response plan is triggered by a test event
Review your AWS CloudTrail configuration for logging security events
common_mistakes: Failing to properly configure CloudWatch Logs
Not testing the incident response plan thoroughly
Ignoring compliance requirements for sensitive data protection

lab.setup: Create a new AWS account and enable the necessary services (CloudFormation, CloudWatch, CloudTrail). Install the AWS CLI and configure your credentials.
steps: Launch an Amazon Linux EC2 instance to serve as a test environment for Sentinel Protocol implementation
Create a new CloudWatch Log group and configure it to capture security events
Set up a simple event pattern in CloudWatch Events to trigger the incident response plan
Test your configuration by simulating a security breach using the AWS CLI
Review your AWS CloudTrail logs for any changes made during the exercise
safety: Do not use production credentials for testing or exercises
Keep your AWS CLI credentials secure and up-to-date
Regularly review and update your incident response plan to ensure it remains effective

bug_injection.description: Inject a simulated security breach into the AWS environment to test the incident response plan.
bug_injection.bad_state: CloudWatch Logs is not configured correctly, leading to incomplete event data.

interrogation_questions: How do you configure CloudWatch Logs to capture security events?
What is the primary goal of an incident response plan in AWS?
Can you describe a scenario where Sentinel Protocol implementation would be particularly beneficial?

accessibility.alt_text_summary: This lesson covers the Sentinel Protocol, a proactive approach to defensive operations using AWS CloudWatch Logs and CloudWatch Events.

resume_bullets: Configured AWS CloudWatch Logs for security event detection
Created an incident response plan with AWS CloudWatch Events
Simulated a security breach to test incident response plan effectiveness
